text.p: Dairy and food group National Foods Ltd said on Tuesday it plans to seek an acquisition within the next 12 to 18 months.

"I would feel uncomfortable if within the next 12 to 18 months we had not replaced the earnings stream that NationalPak offered us," managing director Max Ould managing director told reporters when asked about future acquisitions.
National Foods sold its NationalPak business to First Brands Corp of the U.S. for A$206 million in February.
National Foods earlier reported a net loss of A$12.3 million for the six months to December 31.
Ould said National Foods was not carrying out due diligence on any target at present.
Asked if a juice business acquisition was likely in order to give benefits of scale to National Foods juice division, Ould said the company was still evaluating the juice group.
"It's not as easy as saying you would acquire a juice business and therefore it makes all the financial difference to the business," he said.
"We haven't started to evaulate a particular candidate, therefore I can't say whether it's worthwhile or not. But it has to be a clear priority to at least evaluate."
National Foods woul book a A$70 million profit on the sale of NationalPak.
National Foods shares were six cents lower at A$1.44 at 4.05 p.m. (0505 GMT).
